title: Genome Playlists
blurb: This tutorial introduces genome playlists, which are a way of creating and accessing sets of genomes. These might be the genomes you like to work with most, or could be around a particular theme (e.g. livestock, model organisms, humans etc.).

steps.title: Getting started with playlists
steps.body: Genome playlist are an easy way to group a set of genome that are available everytime you launch Ensembl Go. You can have as many playlists as you like and switching between them is easy.

steps.title: Open Genome Selector
steps.body: Genome are created/edited via the Genome Selector. Click on it now.

steps.title: Some demo genomes
steps.body: The genome list has been populated with some demo genomes: 4 turtles, a rat, a human a, rhino and a warthog.

steps.title: The playlist icon
steps.body: Each genome row has a playlist icon on the far right hand side.

steps.title: Adding genomes to a playlist
steps.body: Here we're going to try adding the 4 turtles to a single playlist. Start by selecting the four highlighted checkboxes for the turtle genomes.

steps.title: Active genomes
steps.body: Now we can see the four genomes appear in the top bar of the app.

Now that we have selected our genomes, we can use this button to add all selected genomes simultaneously to a playlist. We could use the icons on each genome row (regardless of whether a genome is select) to individually  add the genomes to a playlist, but this is quicker when we want to add multiple genomes to a playlist. Try clicking the button now.
steps.title: Adding selected genomes to a playlist
The playlist dialog
steps.body: This box allows us to add the selected genomes to either existing playlists or create a new one. In our case we don't have any existing playlists so we'll create a new one.

steps.title: Name the playlist
steps.body: The only required info is a playlist name, let's call this playlist "Turtles". Enter the name into the box and hit Next to continue.

steps.title: Add a description
steps.body: A description is optional, but are useful if you have a lot of different playlists, particularly when there are overlapping sets of genomes. Try adding a description and then click Next to continue.

steps.title: Save the playlist
steps.body: To finish creating the new playlist, click the 'Add genomes' button below. If we were adding genomes to an existing playlist, this button would become active once one or more existing playlists were selected.

steps.title: The Genome Playlists panel
steps.body: This panel is used to view an manage playlists. The first entry, 'All genomes', is not actually a playlist. It's the default selection for Genome Selector and selecting it shows (but doesn't select) all local genomes in the genome list section. Selecting an actual playlist here will both set the genomes pills on the top bar to match the playlist and filter the genome list in Genome Selector to just those genomes.

steps.title: The Playlist action button
steps.body: The easiest way to select/switch playlist is to use the Playlist action button. This button is accessible from anywhere in the Ensembl Go app and clicking it drops down a list of available playlists. There will also be a 'Previous session' playlist automatically created based on the genomes you had active when you last closed the Ensembl Go app.

steps.title: Clear the selected genomes pill buttons
steps.body: To demonstrate loading a playlist, use the highlighted icons to remove the 4 genomes from the top bar. This also has the effect of deselecting them in Genome Selector.

steps.title: Loading the playlist
steps.body: With the four genomes removed, we're now going to re-select them using the Playlist action button.

steps.title: Chose the Turtles playlist
steps.body: Every playlist you have is listed here, though we only have one for the moment. Click on 'Turtles' to re-select the four turtle genomes

steps.title: Check the top bar
steps.body: You should now see the four turtle genome pill buttons in the top bar above. As selected genomes these buttons will be present in every view of the view of the app until the playlist is changed or they're manually de-selected.

steps.title: A second playlist
steps.body: To demonstrate switching playlists, we're going to create another playlist with things that are not turtles, i.e. the rat, the human, the rhinoceros and the warthog.

steps.title: A click the add all to playlist button
steps.body: We use the same button as before to all four at once. Again, we could add each genome individually with the playlist icons on their corresponding rows, but this is faster since they're all getting added to one list.

steps.title: Name it Not turtles
steps.body: Name the playlist 'Not turtles' and click Next.

steps.title: Create it
steps.body: This time we'll skip adding a description and just add the genomes to the new playlist using the 'Add genomes' button.

steps.title: The Not turtles set
steps.body: Our four non-turtle genomes are now present in the top bar.

playlists.description: Everything else in the tutorial set.

steps.title: Switching between them
steps.body: Now use the Playlist action button to show the two playlists.

steps.title: Both playlists
steps.body: Both playlists are listed, and the tick mark beside 'Not turtles' shows that it is the currently loaded playlist in terms of the selected genomes.

playlists.name: Not turtles
playlists.description: Everything else in the tutorial set.

steps.title: Switch to Turtles
steps.body: Now try clicking 'Turtles' to change the playlist and as a result the selected genomes.

playlists.name: Not turtles
playlists.description: Everything else in the tutorial set.

steps.title: The turtles are back
steps.body: The top bar now shows the four turtle genomes once again.

playlists.name: Not turtles
playlists.description: Everything else in the tutorial set.

steps.title: Editing and deleting
steps.body: Back in the Genome Playlists panel, both playlists are listed. The pencil icon renames a playlist or changes which genomes are in it while the bin icon deletes it. Deleting a playlist never removes the genomes themselves , only the set.

steps.title: Genome playlists tutorial complete
steps.body: You should now be familiar most of the genome playlist functionality. You can experiment with your own genomes of interest in terms of editing/expanding existing playlists.
